subject: PLAN2.P5.3

cases.assertions: Owner commits, deferred local journal failure, unknown and same-key lookup; SQL replay trigger forbids any further owner write.
Unsupported high-risk execute denied before IO; existing ambiguous intent retained for manual workflow, never retried.
Native same-key duplicate returns original outcome; changed hash and changes to accepted outcome/receipt are rejected.
Authenticated host authority verifies evidence/basis; denied authority and malformed basis cannot resolve; journal records operator/evidence refs.
Owner commits and response is lost; takeover preserves original key/request, stale acceptance denied, current epoch confirms once.
Separate owner connection verifies immutable intent committed and local transaction idle; read-before-write probes authoritative absence.
Unknown lookup never becomes absence; wrong operation binding cannot be accepted or replayed.
Lost failure response remains unknown until lookup proves known failure, preserving reservation disposition.
DB-clock backoff, three-attempt cap and cancellation independently deny writes.
Journal rebuild restores deleted direct-action projection; foreign session, wrong digest and revoked owner permission fail closed.
Native retry of unknown uses original key/hash, preserves one owner operation and bounded attempt counter.
Authoritative absent allows same-key recovery; capability mismatch denies before lookup/send.
Actual SIGKILL at advisory-lock barrier after separate owner commit; applying/unknown survives restart, lookup recovers with owner writes forbidden.
Two PHP processes overlap at PostgreSQL lock barrier, then independently reconcile to one confirmation and one owner operation.
Pinned maxAttempts=1 denies native replay; current registry/emergency policy denial stops owner lookup before IO.

limitations: Synthetic owner contracts, not external owner qualification.
Unsupported owner high-risk IO is denied; timeout state is a pre-existing ambiguous-intent fixture, not an unsafe unsupported owner call.
No money owner is implemented; reservation retention is a technical checkpoint and no release is performed.
